title: perf-canary: adaptive sensitivity + hysteresis for auto-detection and rollout guards
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: We observe a large number of transient latency spikes being classified as regressions by the perf canary detector, which results in noisy rollouts and unnecessary rollbacks. This change improves the auto-detection sensitivity by making thresholds adaptive to recent baseline variance and adds hysteresis to rollout guard decisions to reduce flip-flopping during marginal regressions.

What this PR does: implements an adaptive threshold estimator (EWMA-based) that adjusts the detection sensitivity based on recent request latency distribution; introduces per-canary hysteresis windows and minimum observation durations before triggering automatic rollback; exposes two new config knobs: `canary_detection_alpha` (EWMA smoothing) and `canary_hysteresis_ms` (minimum sustained deviation ms), and a safety cap to avoid overly loose thresholds during low-traffic windows.

Design notes: The adaptive estimator maintains EWMA(mean) and EWMA(variance) for the primary latency metric and computes a dynamic threshold = EWMA(mean) + k * sqrt(EWMA(variance)), where k is derived from target false-positive rate. Hysteresis is implemented as a state machine: OK -> WARNING (starts timer) -> FAIL (rollback) only if deviation persists for hysteresis window. We also add a cooldown period after automated rollback to prevent immediate re-promote.

Compatibility: Backwards-compatible defaults preserve current static thresholds if config is not set; rollout guard APIs unchanged. Configs are landed behind a feature flag `perf_canary_adaptive_v2` and can be toggled per-environment.

Testing and results: unit tests for estimator, state transitions; synthetic replay tests showing ~42% reduction in false positive detections on the 30-day latency trace (internal test corpus). Canary e2e shows smoother traffic shifts during a controlled spike injection test (no extra rollout churn).

Checklist:
- [x] Implement estimator and hysteresis state machine
- [x] Unit tests for estimator and state transitions
- [x] Integration canary e2e test
- [x] Feature flag and config docs
- [x] Metrics + dashboard updates

Notes for reviewers: focus on estimator stability (alpha selection), behavior under very low qps, and interactions with KV cache warmup patterns. See linked Linear items for performance analysis and tuning guidance.

review_comments: Liam Chen (reviewer): Overall looks solid. A few questions: how did you pick the default alpha and k values? We should avoid tuning that causes slow reaction to real regressions.

Author (Maya Patel): Default alpha=0.2 and k=3 chosen after running grid search on the 30-day trace (see ENG-8123). Alpha provides a good balance between responsiveness and noise suppression; we expose the knobs for customers and ops to tune per workload.
Sofia Alvarez (reviewer): Danger area is low QPS (<20). EWMA variance can be misleading. Can we fall back to static thresholds when sample count < N?
Author (Maya Patel): Good point. Implemented a minimum-samples gate: if observed samples < 50 over the window we fall back to configured static thresholds. Added tests to cover this path.

Rajesh Kumar (reviewer): CI e2e was flaky initially (timeout). After increasing the job timeout and adding deterministic fixtures the runs are stable. Approving pending one small comment on metric labels consistency.
Maya Patel (author): Addressed metric label naming and added changelog entry in docs. Re-ran perf e2e; green.
release_notes: Improve perf canary detection: adaptive EWMA-based thresholds and hysteresis reduce false positives and stabilize automatic rollouts. Feature is behind `perf_canary_adaptive_v2` feature flag.
